title: Large Language Models for Scientific Publishing: Please, Do Not Make Them a Foe
methodology: The authors created a detection tool by manually identifying 20 predictive features (e.g., paragraph length, sentence complexity, punctuation use, term diversity) and trained it on a dataset of 64 Science Perspective articles and 128 ChatGPT‑generated examples, with test sets of 30 Perspective articles and 60 ChatGPT examples; they later evaluated it on Introduction sections of 13 chemistry journals.
advantages: The tool achieved very high detection performance, exceeding 99% accuracy on full documents and 98–100% accuracy on chemistry journal introductions.
disadvantages: The study is limited to Science Perspective articles and specific journal introductions, which may not represent typical research articles; future LLMs (e.g., GPT‑4) may close the stylistic gap, reducing detection effectiveness.
critique: Relying on handcrafted linguistic features may not scale to diverse writing styles or newer LLMs that can mimic human prose more closely, suggesting the approach could quickly become obsolete without continual feature redesign.
datasets: Science Perspective articles (64 training, 30 test); ChatGPT‑generated examples (128 training, 60 test); Introduction sections of 13 chemistry journals
results: Detection accuracy >99% on full documents; 98%–100% accuracy on chemistry journal introductions.
limitations: Only evaluated on Perspective articles and chemistry introductions; may not generalize to other article types or to newer LLMs like GPT‑4 that address previously identified shortcomings.

title: A Tale of Evaluating Factual Consistency: Case Study on Long Document Summarization Evaluation
methodology: We conduct a systematic study of diverse factual-consistency evaluation systems across four long-document datasets, comparing fine-grained continuous scores to binary classification and examining the relationship between sentence-level and summary-level model performance.
advantages: Fine-grained continuous scores provide more reliable assessments of evaluation systems' capabilities than binary classification.
disadvantages: Advanced systems achieve higher recall for older summaries but struggle with false positives and fine-grained error detection.
critique: The study relies solely on automated, reference‑free metrics without human validation, which may limit confidence in the reported reliability of fine‑grained scores.
results: Fine-grained continuous scores are more reliable than binary classification; advanced systems have higher recall on older summaries but exhibit false positives and difficulty with fine-grained error detection.
extraction_note: abstract only; no detailed methods, datasets, metrics, or explicit limitations provided

title: Formal model of multi-agent architecture of a software system based on knowledge interpretation
methodology: The study employs formal methods, specifically closed path rules and predicate logic, to develop a multi-agent system architecture composed of five distinct agents for rule extraction and knowledge interpretation.
advantages: The agent-based paradigm offers a decentralized, autonomous, and scalable framework for handling large and complex knowledge repositories, enabling dynamic interpretation of vast knowledge bases.
critique: The paper describes a formal framework and system architecture but provides no empirical evaluation, datasets, or quantitative metrics to substantiate the claimed benefits, making it difficult to assess practical effectiveness.
results: A rule mining approach based on closed path rules for processing extensive datasets, a formalization of relevance to automatically exclude irrelevant fragments, and the realization of a multi-agent system with five agents dedicated to rule extraction and knowledge interpretation.
extraction_note: abstract only; no detailed experimental sections, datasets, or metrics provided

title: Structured PREreview of "An Exploratory Study of Code Retrieval Techniques in Coding Agents"
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
methodology: Qualitative exploratory study using a single coding task and repository, running multiple coding agents (lexical, hybrid, AST/graph, multi‑agent) with repeated trials to capture LLM non‑determinism, collecting execution traces, qualitative observations, and quantitative measures such as token usage, tool calls, costs, and completion status.
advantages: Provides a structured comparison of diverse coding agents with transparent execution traces and reproducible appendices, enabling hypothesis generation about retrieval approaches.
disadvantages: Limited external validity due to a single task/repository, confounding variables (different models, prompts, tools) not isolated, lack of controlled ablations, no standardized retrieval metrics, and absence of statistical analysis.
critique: While the study offers valuable exploratory insights, the lack of rigorous experimental controls and statistical evaluation makes it difficult to draw reliable causal conclusions about the effectiveness of retrieval techniques.
metrics: tokens; tool calls; costs; completion status
results: Findings include no clear win for semantic search, LSP adding overhead without gains, multi‑agent setups showing low token use but coordination overhead, and a trade‑off between transparency and efficiency; AST/graph methods appear to outperform others but conclusions are tentative due to limited scope.
limitations: Single task and repository scope, confounding variables across agents, no standardized retrieval metrics, and lack of statistical significance testing limit the generalizability of the conclusions.

title: Generating (Factual?) Narrative Summaries of RCTs: Experiments with\n Neural Multi-Document Summarization
methodology: Automatically generate a narrative biomedical evidence summary from multiple trial reports by evaluating modern neural abstractive summarization models on article abstracts from systematic reviews, using the authors' conclusions section of the review abstract as the target summary.
advantages: Modern summarization systems produce consistently fluent and relevant synopses, and domain‑specific strategies modestly improve factual accuracy.
disadvantages: The generated summaries are not always factual.
critique: The study evaluates summarization only on abstracts from systematic reviews, which may omit important details from full trial reports, limiting the assessment of factual completeness and real‑world applicability.
results: Modern summarization systems yield fluent and relevant synopses but are not always factual; domain‑specific strategies modestly improve factual accuracy of the generated summaries.

title: Tuning RAG: When Retrieval Helps vs. Hurts
methodology: Four control levers for tuning retrieval aggressiveness: similarity score cutoffs, dynamic top‑k tuning, model‑gated retrieval, and prompt framing that preserves generative agency.
advantages: Conservative retrieval (e.g., similarity thresholds, model‑gated retrieval) preserves the model's reasoning and synthesis abilities, avoiding the shift to a search‑engine mode.
disadvantages: Over‑retrieval (low similarity thresholds, high top‑k) floods the model with context, suppressing its core strengths and leading to poor performance on reasoning or novel combination tasks.
critique: The discussion is purely conceptual and lacks empirical validation on concrete datasets or benchmarks, making it unclear how the proposed levers perform in practice.
limitations: The text provides only a high‑level overview without experimental results, datasets, or quantitative metrics.
extraction_note: Only an episode summary is available; no full paper text, datasets, or quantitative results.

methodology: Comparative analysis of EDA summaries produced by human analysts versus those generated by large language models, evaluated across four dimensions: factual accuracy, analytical completeness, expression of uncertainty, and perceived analytical trustworthiness.
advantages: AI-generated summaries offer speed and scalability; hybrid human‑AI workflows can enhance reliability, openness, and credibility of EDA‑based decision support.
disadvantages: AI summaries may suffer from lower interpretive accuracy, incomplete statements about uncertainty, and risk misinterpretation or decision bias due to inaccuracies and poor communication of uncertainty.
critique: The paper outlines evaluation dimensions but provides no concrete datasets, quantitative results, or empirical validation, making it difficult to assess the practical significance of the claimed benefits and drawbacks.

title: SourceMinds at CheckThat! 2026: NLI-Grounded Citation Auditing in a Multi-Agent Pipeline for Full Fact-Checking Article Generation
methodology: Multi-agent pipeline combining evidence retrieval (dense retrieval, reranking, source-balanced selection), structured fact planning, article generation, a gated self-critique stage to revise weakly grounded drafts, and an NLI-based citation auditor that repairs missing citations and removes unsupported or redundant ones.
critique: The described pipeline involves many sequential components, which may increase system complexity and runtime latency, and the abstract provides no empirical evidence of how each stage contributes to overall performance.
